questions.text: A proposed residential development in an URBAN area is adjacent to a creek. Under PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Article 51, what public-use easement applies along the creek bank?

options.text: 3 meters
10 meters
20 meters
40 meters

rationale.a: Correct. PD 1067 Article 51 establishes a 3-meter public-use easement along banks of rivers/streams and shores of seas/lakes in URBAN areas.
rationale.b: Wrong. 10 meters is not an Article 51 figure.
rationale.c: Wrong. 20 meters applies in AGRICULTURAL areas, not urban.
rationale.d: Wrong. 40 meters applies in FOREST areas, not urban.
rationale.correct: PD 1067 Article 51: easement of public use is 3 m in urban areas, 20 m in agricultural areas, and 40 m in forest areas. For an urban creek, the easement is 3 meters and no permanent structures may be built within it.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1067 easements are determined by LAND CLASSIFICATION (urban/agricultural/forest), NOT by stream width. The 'streams less than 6 m require 3 m' rule found in some reviewers is fabricated.

questions.explanation: When existing drainage infrastructure is insufficient, on-site stormwater management (retention/detention) is standard practice to control runoff and prevent downstream flooding. This is now a core site planning component. Overloading an already-insufficient system is not a responsible solution. Elevation is a complementary flood mitigation strategy but does not address the root drainage problem. Density reduction addresses runoff volume but is not required if on-site stormwater management is designed. When existing drainage infrastructure is insufficient, on-site stormwater management (retention/detention) is standard practice to control runoff and prevent downstream flooding. This is now a core site planning component. Insufficient drainage capacity requires on-site stormwater management (detention/retention) as part of site design.
